Emma — thanks for the clear list. See answers inline and referenced attachments; we'll follow up with a short call to walk through operational details.

High-level answers:
- Replication model and classes:
  * Critical control plane & metadata (tenant config, model pins): synchronous cross-AZ replication within region; target RPO = 0 for control-plane state.
  * Customer request/usage data (request logs, token traces): asynchronous cross-region replication (multi-minute typical lag); designed RPO for request logs is <= 5 minutes for most tiers, configurable tighter for Dedicated customers.
  * Persistent model artifacts & snapshots: object-store replication with versioned artifacts; RPO = 0 for model artifacts because we maintain immutable model versions and geo-replicated storage.

- RTO commitments (typical):
  * Full regional failover to warm standby: targeted RTO = 60 minutes for hosted API baseline; 30 minutes for Dedicated SLA commitments (per contract).
  * Single-service failover (stateless frontend): usually < 5 minutes with automated routing.

- Snapshot / PITR for encrypted volumes: we support encrypted snapshots (KMS-managed). Snapshot frequency for control-plane/config is hourly by default; customers can opt for higher cadence. Point-in-time restore supported for DB-backed metadata (up to 7 days retention by default, configurable).

Evidence / artifacts provided: Redwood_DR_Evidence_Package_v2.zip (contains runbook excerpts, last rehearsal log, redacted audit trails). Also linked: https://drive.google.com/redwood/hydebank/dr-evidence

Emma — Monica here from Customer Success, following up with the consolidated artifacts and an explicit sequencing extract. Apologies for the delay; we pulled the rehearsal artifacts and produced the acceptance criteria table you requested.

Runbook extract (sequencing summary for full-region failover -> warm standby -> cutover):
1) Detection & Triage (0-2 minutes): automated monitoring flags region outage; on-call notified via PagerDuty; validation by NOC (confirm metrics and synthetic probe failures).
2) Pre-failover checks (2-10 minutes): verify control-plane integrity, validate latest KV checkpoint age (we maintain sequence numbers and last-applied index); ensure replicas in standby region are healthy.
3) Traffic re-routing (10-25 minutes): update routing policy -> DNS TTL pre-warm step (we use split-horizon DNS and traffic steering); warm caches by replaying recent prefix/KV snapshots to instances in standby region.
4) State sync & consistency window (25-45 minutes): apply any outstanding asynchronous log segments; for Dedicated customers that require RPO=0 we recommend hybrid synchronous replication for the critical subset prior to cutover; validate checksum/asserts.
5) Cutover & sanity checks (45-60 minutes): mark standby as active, ramp capacity, run smoke tests (end-to-end generation on sample prompts, embedding verification).
6) Post-cutover validation (60-90 minutes): monitor latency, error rates, per-route token throughput; roll back if regressions exceed thresholds defined in acceptance criteria.

Per-step expected timing (typical hosted baseline vs Dedicated SLA):
- Detection: ~0-2m (both)
- Pre-failover checks: 8-12m (hosted) / 4-6m (Dedicated ops playbook)
- Routing + warm caches: 10-20m (hosted) / 5-10m (Dedicated)
- Final sync + cutover: up to 30m (hosted) / 10-15m (Dedicated)

Evidence of rehearsal: last full-region rehearsal executed 2026-09-21 (log snippet inside Redwood_DR_Evidence_Package_v2.zip, file: rehearsal-20260921.log). Outcome: warm-standby cutover completed in 38 minutes (observed), with two minor runbook refinements (cache warming order and KV checkpoint alignment) remedied post-run. We included the redacted post-mortem in the evidence package.

KMS/BYOK notes: we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). For BYOK cross-region restores: snapshots remain encrypted with the customer key; to restore in standby region you must authorize cross-region key use (we provide a documented flow and support for key policy automation). If cross-region key policies are not permitted by your KMS rules, we recommend an export-and-rewrap approach facilitated by our key escrow option under an agreed SOP (detailed in the attachment).

Acceptance test criteria (pass/fail highlights):
- RTO verification: inbound traffic routed and e2e request success rate >= 99% of baseline within agreed RTO window.
- RPO verification: spot-check of recent token logs shows no more than allowed data window loss (<= configured RPO).
- Performance verification: 95th percentile latency for representative prompt set must be within 20% of pre-failover baseline for Dedicated; within 2x for hosted baseline.
- Rollback trigger: error rate > 5% sustained for 5 minutes or 95th percentile latency > 3x baseline.
